metadata.title: Raise a ValueError
metadata.description: Define a function that raises ValueError for invalid arguments instead of printing an error.

instructions.main: Define `withdraw(amount)`: return the amount when it is not negative, and raise `ValueError` when it is negative.
steps: Guard the invalid case: `if amount < 0: raise ValueError("amount must not be negative")`.
Raise the error — a function_state call to `withdraw(-1)` checks that the exact exception type is `ValueError`.

hints.message: Define `def withdraw(amount):` and end the negative branch with `raise ValueError(...)`.
Printing an error message is not raising one — the caller cannot catch a print. Use `raise ValueError("amount must not be negative")` so the invalid amount stops the program.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: withdraw returns valid amounts and raises ValueError for negative ones.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: For a negative amount, raise `ValueError` — printing an error or returning normally is not enough.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: You raise ValueError in the invalid branch.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Raise the error with `raise ValueError("amount must not be negative")` — don't print an error message.
